chunks: "The morning sleep is inauspicious: it drives away sustenance, causes the complexion to pale, makes it ugly, and changes it. It is the sleep of every unfortunate one. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, distributes sustenance between the rising of al-Fajr and the rising of the sun, so beware of that sleep."

key_terms.الرِّزْقَ: sustenance and provision granted by Allah
key_terms.الْأَرْزَاقَ: the various provisions apportioned to people
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the early morning, especially the time after dawn
key_terms.فَإِيَّاكُمْ: so beware; a warning to avoid something
key_terms.مَشْؤُومَةٌ: inauspicious and a cause of misfortune
key_terms.نَوْمَةُ: a single act or period of sleep

ai.seo_question: Why is sleeping after al-Fajr considered disliked in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام warns against sleeping in the early morning after al-Fajr. The hadith links this habit to deprivation in livelihood and presents the period between dawn and sunrise as a time in which Allah, Blessed and Exalted, apportions sustenance.
